subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: The arrangement of elements within an artwork
The size of the canvas only
questions.explain: Composition is how the visual elements are arranged and organised within the picture area.

questions.q: Two-point perspective uses how many vanishing points?
questions.explain: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points on the horizon, typically for objects seen at a corner.

questions.q: In a landscape, objects placed at the bottom of the picture usually appear to be in the...
questions.explain: Objects lower in the picture plane normally read as nearer to the viewer, in the foreground.

questions.q: Which 3D technique is additive, building up a form from a soft material?
questions.explain: Modelling adds and shapes pliable material such as clay to build up a form.

questions.q: What does adding white to a colour create?
questions.explain: Adding white to a colour produces a tint (a lighter version), while adding black produces a shade.

questions.q: Collage is an artwork made by...
options: Sticking different materials onto a surface
questions.explain: Collage assembles and glues various materials, such as paper or fabric, onto a surface.

options: A small preliminary model of a sculpture
questions.explain: A maquette is a small-scale model made to plan and test ideas for a larger sculpture.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a sketchbook in GCSE Art?
options: To record ideas and show development of work
questions.explain: A sketchbook records observations, experiments and the development of ideas towards a final piece.

questions.q: A 'hue' refers to which property of colour?
options: The pure colour itself, such as red or blue
questions.explain: Hue is the name of the pure colour, such as red, yellow or blue, before tints or shades are added.

options: Thick paint applied with a knife
A thin, transparent layer of diluted paint
questions.explain: A wash is a thin, transparent layer of watercolour spread over an area to build colour gradually.

questions.q: What is the key difference between shape and form?
options: Shape is two-dimensional, form is three-dimensional
Shape is large, form is small
Shape is coloured, form is not
questions.explain: A shape is flat and two-dimensional, while a form has depth and appears three-dimensional.

questions.q: What is the secondary colour made by mixing red and yellow?
questions.explain: Red mixed with yellow produces the secondary colour orange.
